rationale: Marginal label alignment discards a modality even when joint descriptors help. Instead retain complementary feature components by kernel ridge residualisation, without aligning modality weights to labels.
source: Fixed DINOv2 global RGB/depth descriptors and existing animal-group splits
projection: For target-feature kernel K_R and predictor kernel K_D, A=(K_D+eta I)^-1. The residual feature at x is phi_R(x)-k_D(x,X) A Phi_R(X). The residual kernel is the corresponding inner product, so it is PSD; all projection anchors are training episodes only.
normalisation: Normalise residual kernel entries by square root of corresponding residual self-kernel diagonals, with lower bound 1e-12
fusion: Equal convex sum of base and residual kernels, or two residual kernels; no label-based removal of a modality
SVR: C=1/alpha, epsilon=.1; inner-validation MAE chooses settings; source test outcomes from earlier development are known, so later comparisons remain exploratory
mismatch: Permute depth training anchors relative to RGB targets only for the cross-modal projection. Keep the base depth kernel and true BCS regression labels unchanged. Save mapping.
claims: Shared features are statistically predictable features, not verified background or nuisance variables. Residualisation does not identify anatomy or causal factors. Kernel ridge residualisation is an existing construction; this is an application-specific fusion candidate.
